$comment: Single source of truth for the structure of data.csv: field names, types, descriptions (the data dictionary rendered on wildeshortfiction.com/about) and the row checks run on every push by .github/workflows/validate.yml. Citation metadata lives in CITATION.cff, not here.
name: wilde-short-fiction
title: Wilde Short Fiction: Contemporary Reviews of Oscar Wilde's Short Story Collections

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier of the record. It is also the address of the record's page on the website (/reviews/{id}).

fields.name: transcription
fields.description: Manual transcription of the item. See Transcription in METHODOLOGY.md for the conventions (asterisks for italics, [sic], square brackets for editorial additions).

fields.name: collection
fields.description: The collection or collections the item discusses; several are joined by ", ". To filter by collection, use the collection_* columns.

constraints.pattern: ^(The Happy Prince and Other Tales|Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories|A House of Pomegranates)(, (The Happy Prince and Other Tales|Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories|A House of Pomegranates))*$

fields.name: collection_hp
fields.description: "y" if the item discusses The Happy Prince and Other Tales, otherwise "n".

fields.name: collection_lasc
fields.description: "y" if the item discusses Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories, otherwise "n".

fields.name: collection_ahop
fields.description: "y" if the item discusses A House of Pomegranates, otherwise "n".

fields.name: period
fields.description: Chronological group by date of publication: 1 is the first reception of the collections (to 31 March 1895); 2 runs from Wilde's trials (April 1895) to 30 November 1900; 3 is after Wilde's death.

fields.name: publication_type
fields.description: Kind of item: a contemporary review (original or reprint), a notice, a news item mentioning a collection without reviewing it, an article, a letter (correspondence), an obituary, or an advertisement. See Scope in METHODOLOGY.md.

fields.name: publication_year
fields.description: Year of publication.

fields.name: publication_month
fields.description: Month of publication (1–12), where known.

fields.name: publication_day
fields.description: Day of publication, where known.

fields.name: publication_name
fields.description: Name of the periodical.

fields.name: publication_country
fields.description: Country where the periodical was published.

fields.name: publication_region
fields.description: Region within the country where the periodical was published.

fields.name: publication_place
fields.description: Town or city where the periodical was published.

fields.name: publication_volume
fields.description: Volume of the periodical, as printed (Arabic or Roman numerals).

fields.name: publication_number
fields.description: Issue number of the periodical.

fields.name: publication_pages
fields.description: Page or page range of the item.

fields.name: publication_reviewer
fields.description: Reviewer, where identified. Most Victorian reviews were unsigned, so this is usually empty.

fields.name: archive_name
fields.description: Digitised collection where the item was found.

fields.name: archive_url
fields.description: Link to the item in that collection. Some collections require a subscription.

fields.name: accessed
fields.description: Date the source was consulted (YYYY-MM-DD).

fields.name: transcribed
fields.description: Date the transcription was completed (YYYY-MM-DD).

fields.name: comments
fields.description: Editorial notes on the record.

fields.name: citekey
fields.description: Citation key of the record, used in reference managers and as the key of its item in the project's Zotero group. Built from the periodical's code and the date of publication; unlike id, it can change when a possible duplicate is resolved.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description: Links records that are not independent: W = the same text printed in several periodicals; L = letters that answer one another; Q = a text that quotes another record. Empty when the record is in no chain. See Reprints and chains in METHODOLOGY.md.
